title: auth/header: scoped tokens, CORS relaxations, request-signing nonce semantics
author: Priya Sharma
description: Motivation: clarify and standardize Authorization header semantics across Redwood's API surface (hosted/OpenAI-compat/SDKs) to support project/org keys, short-lived scoped tokens for browser usage, CORS header requirements, and request signing (nonce) semantics for Private/VPC deployments. Summary: - Accept both legacy 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' and new scoped token formats. Scoped tokens encode scope metadata and are validated server-side; SDKs updated to mint and refresh short-lived scopes. - Add optional request-signing headers 'X-Redwood-Nonce' and 'X-Redwood-Signature' for private deployments and webhook validation; semantics documented and replay protection enforced (nonce TTL). - CORS: document recommended pattern for browser usage (use short-lived scoped tokens via a backend exchange or the new 'x-redwood-scoped-token' header). Updated Access-Control-Allow-Headers to include 'X-Redwood-Nonce' and 'X-Redwood-Signature' when request-signing is enabled; explicit guidance to avoid exposing long-lived project/org keys in browser apps. - OpenAI-compat: ensure compatibility layer continues to accept 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' for existing clients and accepts the 'Redwood-Project <proj_key>' and 'Redwood-Org <org_key>' header forms when present. - SDKs/docs: added code samples and migration notes for Python/TS/Go. - Tests: added unit tests for header parsing, nonce replay protection, CORS behavior, and integration test validating OpenAI-compat header acceptance. See changes for file list and commit summaries below.

review_comments: Casey Nguyen: Asked for explicit behavior when both Authorization and Redwood-Project headers are present; requested precedence rules and unit tests.
Priya Sharma: Responded that explicit precedence is: Redwood-Project/Redwood-Org take precedence over Bearer when present and that logic is covered in new header parsing unit tests.
Jordan Lee: Requested clarity around CORS exposure of Authorization vs custom header; asked to add guidance to docs about exchanging long-lived keys on backend.
Priya Sharma: Added docs snippet and expanded migration guide per request.
Marta Ruiz: Requested performance consideration for nonce store; suggested in-memory LRU backing with optional redis for multi-instance deployments.
Priya Sharma: Implemented in-memory LRU default and pluggable redis backend; added config knobs and tests.
release_notes: Stabilizes Authorization header semantics: supports scoped short-lived tokens (recommended for browser usage), documents CORS guidance, adds optional request-signing headers (X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Signature) for Private deployments, and keeps OpenAI-compat fallbacks for existing clients. SDK updates included for token helpers.
